newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Atlas Copco sees 1997 profits above '96.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Copco sees 1997 profits above '96.

text.p: Swedish industrial engineer Atlas Copco on Wednesday posted a 10 percent lift in profits in the first half of 1997 and repeated its forecast for a slightly higher profit this year compared to 1996.
It said profit after financial items reached 1.72 billion crowns ($212.2 million) which was slightly above market expectations of 1.55 billion.
Adjusted for non-recurring items of 32 million crowns in the first half of 1997 and 117 million crowns in 1996, profit rose 16 percent, the company said in a statement.

"Despite the initial negative effect of the Prime Service acquisition, our previous forecast of a somewhat higher profit compared to 1996 stands firm," the company said, referring to the US$900 million purchase of a U.S. rental equipment group.
"Demand is expected to remain at the present level for the rest of the year."
In its first quarter report for 1997 Atlas Copco said it saw no change in demand from 1996.
Still, order intake rose 14 percent in the first half of the year and sales advanced 11 percent to 13.78 billion crowns.
Foreign exchange rate fluctuations, primarily the stronger dollar, had a positive effect of about six percent on both sales and orders.
"Significant (order) increases were noted in Japan, China, Australia, South America as well as in southern Europe and Britain," Atlas Copco said.
"Sales of compressors, advanced industrial power tools and mining equipment showed volume increases."

The company noted that the second quarter had been strong with sales totalling 7.38 billion crowns, up from 6.34 billion crowns in the second quarter of 1996 and from 6.41 billion in the first quarter of this year.
Profit after financial items rose 29 percent to 984 million crowns in the second quarter from a year ago and from 735 million crowns in the first quarter of 1997.

In the first half of 1997, operating profit rose to 1.71 billion crowns from 1.49 billion in the first six months of 1996 and the operating margin edged up to 12.4 percent from 12 percent, lifted by larger volumes and foreign exchange moves.
Earnings per share advanced to 5.80 crowns in the first six months of the year from 5.57 crowns a year earlier.
Net debt fell to 2.06 billion crowns in the first half of 1997 from 3.09 billion with the debt-to-equity ratio falling to 16 percent from 28 percent.
Atlas Copco's share rose ahead of the report and at 1045 GMT was trading at 241 crowns on the Stockholm Stock Exchange, up seven from its Tuesday close but off morning highs of 244 crowns.
